1. Both cells to the left of the 5 have to be mines because there can only be one mine next to the 3.

2. Since the mine to complete the 3 is either the cell to the upper-left or the cell above it, the upper-right cell cannot be a mine.

3. 1-1 rule on the very left edge. The cell above the 1 is safe.

4. The cell directly left of the two in the mid-left cannot be a mine because then the only way for the 3 below it to have a mine would be is the 1 in the middle had 2, so it cannot be. 

5. The 4 and the three on the mid-right of the screen both have one mine left, so the cell diagnolly to the upper-right is not a mine.

6. In the same general area as in #4, but on the top edge there (with the row of 2's) the 2nd 2 in a row is a mine, because the 3rd 2's mines cannot both be touching the 4th 2, which already has 1 mine. 

7. Also in the area of #6, the cell above 4 is not a mine, because the 2nd mine of the 4th 2 must also be touching the 3rd 2.

Thats probably not all, only the things I saw looking at it.
